back: International Union for Conservation of Nature: assesses extinction risk of species and publishes the Red List.

front: IUCN Red List categories (most to least threatened)
back: EX, EW, CR, EN, VU, NT, LC (plus DD, data deficient). CR, EN and VU are 'threatened'.
Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora: regulates international wildlife trade.

front: CITES appendices I, II and III
back: I: commercial trade banned. II: trade with export permit if sustainable. III: protected in one country that asks for help.
A species introduced by humans outside its natural range that spreads and harms native biodiversity or the economy.

front: Five reasons to control invasive species
back: Competition, predation, disease, hybridisation and economic cost.
Prevention (biosecurity), early eradication, mechanical, chemical and biological control.

front: Why must biological control agents be tested?
back: To show they are host-specific, so they will not attack native or crop species and become pests themselves.
IUCN assesses and advises; CITES is a binding agreement controlling international trade.
